operations.specification: Create a new guest account using device fingerprint for anonymous access. Generate a unique guest ID and store the device fingerprint with uniqueness constraint. Create an initial guest session with access and refresh JWT tokens. Return the guest ID and tokens in the response. Handle duplicate device fingerprint by returning existing guest credentials. Validate device_fingerprint is provided and non-empty. Set session expiration based on configured guest session lifetime.
operations.description:
Register a new guest account for anonymous access to public endpoints. This operation creates a guest identity using the provided device fingerprint, which serves as a unique identifier for tracking anonymous users across sessions.

The device fingerprint is stored with a uniqueness constraint to ensure each device maintains a single guest account. If a guest account already exists for the provided fingerprint, the operation returns the existing credentials rather than creating a duplicate.

Upon successful registration, the system generates a new guest session with both access and refresh JWT tokens. The access token grants immediate authorization to protected endpoints, while the refresh token enables token renewal without re-registration. Session metadata including client IP, referrer, and current page URL are recorded for security auditing.

Guest accounts support soft deletion via the deleted_at timestamp, allowing for account recovery within the retention period. This operation does not require prior authentication as it is the entry point for anonymous users.

requestBody.description: Guest registration request containing device fingerprint for anonymous identification.

responseBody.description: Guest authorization response containing guest ID and JWT tokens for session access.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Refresh an expired access token using a valid refresh token. Validate the refresh token signature and expiration. Check that the associated guest session exists and is not expired. Verify the guest account is active (deleted_at is null). Generate a new access token and optionally a new refresh token. Return the new tokens in the response. Invalidate the old refresh token if token rotation is enabled. Handle expired refresh tokens by returning authentication error.
operations.description:
Renew an expired access token using a valid refresh token for continued guest session access. This operation enables guests to maintain their anonymous session without re-registering.

The refresh token is validated for signature integrity and expiration status. The associated guest session is checked to ensure it exists in the database and has not exceeded its expiration timestamp. The guest account itself is verified to be active by confirming the deleted_at field is null.

Upon successful validation, a new access token is generated with updated expiration. Optionally, a new refresh token may be issued if token rotation is enabled for enhanced security. The old refresh token is invalidated in rotation scenarios to prevent token reuse.

This operation uses the refresh token itself as the authorization mechanism. Failed refresh attempts due to expired or invalid tokens return appropriate authentication errors, requiring the client to re-register via the join endpoint.

requestBody.description: Token refresh request containing the refresh token for session renewal.

responseBody.description: Guest authorization response containing renewed JWT tokens for continued session access.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Register a new member account with email and password. Validate email format and uniqueness, hash password with bcrypt, create member record in multi_user_todo_members table, generate email verification token in multi_user_todo_member_email_verifications, send verification email, create initial session in multi_user_todo_member_sessions with access and refresh tokens. Return tokens and member info. Handle duplicate email (409), invalid email format (400), weak password (400).
operations.description:
Register a new member account with email and password authentication.

This operation creates a new member record in the multi_user_todo_members table with the provided email and bcrypt-hashed password. The email field must be unique across all member accounts. Upon successful registration, an email verification token is generated and stored in multi_user_todo_member_email_verifications for account activation.

The operation returns access and refresh tokens in the IMultiUserTodoMember.IAuthorized response, along with the newly created member's ID. The member can immediately use these tokens to access authenticated endpoints.

Email verification is required to fully activate the account. The verification token expires after a configured period. Members should check their email and complete verification to ensure full account functionality.

requestBody.description: Registration credentials for new member account creation.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and member info for newly registered account.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate member with email and password. Validate credentials against multi_user_todo_members table, verify bcrypt password hash, check account not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null), create session in multi_user_todo_member_sessions with client IP and referrer info, generate JWT access and refresh tokens. Return tokens and member info. Handle invalid credentials (401), unverified email (403), deleted account (403).
operations.description:
Authenticate a member with email and password credentials.

This operation validates the provided email and password against the multi_user_todo_members table. The password is verified using bcrypt hash comparison. The account must not be soft-deleted (deleted_at must be null) to successfully authenticate.

Upon successful authentication, a new session record is created in multi_user_todo_member_sessions with the client's IP address, current page URL, and referrer. JWT access and refresh tokens are generated and returned in the IMultiUserTodoMember.IAuthorized response.

Failed authentication attempts return 401 Unauthorized. Accounts with unverified emails or soft-deleted accounts return 403 Forbidden with appropriate error messages.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and member info for logged-in member.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh access token using valid refresh token. Validate refresh token against multi_user_todo_member_sessions table, check session not expired (expired_at), verify member account exists and is not deleted, generate new access token and optionally new refresh token, update session expired_at. Return new tokens. Handle invalid refresh token (401), expired session (401), deleted account (403).
operations.description:
Refresh authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This operation validates the provided refresh token against existing sessions in the multi_user_todo_member_sessions table. The session must not be expired (expired_at must be in the future) and the associated member account must exist and not be soft-deleted.

Upon successful validation, new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated. The session's expired_at timestamp is updated to extend the session duration. The new tokens are returned in the IMultiUserTodoMember.IAuthorized response.

This operation enables seamless session continuation without requiring re-authentication. Refresh tokens should be securely stored by clients and rotated on each use for enhanced security.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens for continued session.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of active user sessions for administrative monitoring.

This operation provides session visibility for system administrators, including member and guest sessions with filtering by creation date, expiration status, and session metadata. Sessions are automatically created during authentication and cannot be manually modified.

Response includes session summary information with IP addresses, creation timestamps, and expiration times. This endpoint is restricted to administrative users only.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query session tables (multi_user_todo_member_sessions and multi_user_todo_guest_sessions) with pagination and filtering. This is an admin-only endpoint for monitoring active sessions. Apply filters on creation date range, expiration status, and actor type (member/guest). Join with member/guest tables for user information if requested. Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Sessions are append-only - no update operations allowed.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for session filtering

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific member session.

This operation returns complete session data including creation timestamp, expiration time, client IP address, and navigation context (href and referrer) captured at session creation. Sessions are private to their owners and cannot be accessed by other users.

The session must belong to the authenticated member making the request. Attempts to access another user's session are rejected with authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query multi_user_todo_member_sessions table by session ID UUID. Verify the session belongs to the authenticated member by checking multi_user_todo_member_id matches the current user's ID. Return full session entity with all fields: id, multi_user_todo_member_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at. Handle case where session doesn't exist or belongs to different user by returning 404 or 403 error.

responseBody.description: Complete session information including timestamps and client context

operations.description:
Retrieve the current authenticated member's profile information including their display name.

This operation returns the profile data for the member associated with the current authentication session. The response includes the user's display name shown in the application interface, along with metadata timestamps for profile creation and last update.

Only authenticated members can access this endpoint. Guest users without valid authentication cannot retrieve profile information. The endpoint enforces strict privacy controls - users can only access their own profile linked to their session, with no ability to view other users' profiles.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query multi_user_todo_user_profiles table for the current authenticated member's profile. Join with multi_user_todo_members using multi_user_todo_member_id to verify the profile belongs to the current session user. Return the profile with display_name, created_at, updated_at fields. Ensure deleted_at is null (active profile only). Reject request if user is not authenticated (guest actor). Reject any attempt to access another user's profile - this endpoint only returns the profile linked to the current session's member ID.

responseBody.description: Current user's profile with display name

operations.description:
Update the current authenticated user's profile information including display name.

This operation allows members to modify their profile display name. The display name is shown throughout the application to identify the user. Profile changes are saved immediately upon submission and take effect for all subsequent operations.

Only the authenticated profile owner can perform this operation. Attempts to access or modify another user's profile are rejected. The display name field is optional and can be updated multiple times without restrictions.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Update the authenticated member's user profile display name. Query multi_user_todo_user_profiles table using the authenticated member's ID from session context (multi_user_todo_member_id). Validate display_name meets requirements: optional field, can be updated multiple times. Update the display_name field and set updated_at timestamp. Return the complete updated profile record. Reject requests if member is not authenticated or attempts to modify another user's profile. The unique constraint on multi_user_todo_member_id ensures one profile per member.

responseBody.description: Updated user profile with new display name

requestBody.description: Profile update data with new display name value

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of the authenticated user's todos.

This operation provides comprehensive todo list browsing with support for completion status filtering (all, complete, or incomplete), multiple sorting options (creation date, start date, due date), and configurable pagination. Users can customize their view to focus on active tasks, completed items, or browse their entire collection.

All todos returned belong exclusively to the authenticated user - the system enforces strict privacy boundaries preventing access to other users' todos. Todos without start or due dates are positioned at the end of sorted lists regardless of sort direction.

The response includes todo summary information optimized for list displays, showing title, completion status, optional dates, and creation timestamp. For full todo details including complete description, use the GET /multiUserTodo/member/todos/{todoId} endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_todos table filtered by the authenticated member's ownership.

Apply completion status filter from request body:
- 'all' or undefined: no status filter
- 'complete': WHERE completed_at IS NOT NULL
- 'incomplete': WHERE completed_at IS NULL

Apply sorting based on request parameters:
- sortBy: 'createdAt', 'startedAt', or 'dueAt'
- sortDirection: 'asc' or 'desc'
- For startedAt/dueAt sorting: NULL values always appear at end regardless of direction

Implement cursor-based or offset pagination with limit and page parameters.
Return paginated results with IMultiUserTodoTodo.ISummary type containing: id, title, completed status, startedAt, dueAt, createdAt.

Verify member session authentication before query execution.
Ensure query scope is restricted to requesting member's todos only (WHERE member_id = current_user_id).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summaries for the authenticated user

requestBody.description: Search criteria including completion status filter, sorting options, and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated member.

This operation allows members to create personal todo items in their private workspace. The todo requires a title and may optionally include a description, start date, and due date. Upon creation, the todo is automatically marked as incomplete (completed_at is null) and associated with the authenticated member's account.

All todos are strictly private to their owner as per the application's data isolation policy. Members cannot access todos belonging to other users. The created todo is returned in the response with all fields including the system-generated UUID identifier and timestamps.

Note: Initial todo creation does not create an edit history entry. Edit history entries are only generated when existing todos are modified.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Insert a new record into multi_user_todo_todos table with the provided title, description, start_date, and due_date fields. Set completed to false by default. Associate the todo with the authenticated member's ID from the session. Set created_at to current timestamp. Return the complete created todo entity including the generated UUID. No edit history entry is created for initial todo creation - history entries are only created on subsequent edit operations.

responseBody.description: The created todo entity with all fields including system-generated UUID and timestamps

requestBody.description: Todo creation data with required title and optional description, start date, and due date

operations.description:
Retrieve a single active todo item by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete todo entity including all fields: title, description, optional start and due dates, completion status, and timestamps. The todo must belong to the authenticated member making the request.

Only active (non-deleted) todos are returned. Todos with deleted_at set (soft-deleted) are excluded from this endpoint and should be accessed via trash-specific endpoints instead.

Returns 404 if the todo does not exist, does not belong to the current user, or has been soft-deleted. All todo endpoints enforce strict ownership - members can only access their own todos.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_todos table by primary key ID.

Verify the todo belongs to the authenticated member by checking multi_user_todo_member_id matches the session's member ID.

Return the full todo entity with all fields: id, title, description, started_at, due_at, completed_at, deleted_at, created_at, updated_at.

If todo not found or ownership verification fails, return 404 Not Found.

Exclude soft-deleted todos (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from normal retrieval - these should only be accessible via trash endpoints.

responseBody.description: Complete todo entity with all fields

operations.description:
Update an existing todo's properties including title, description, start date, and due date.

This operation allows users to modify their own todos by updating any combination of fields. All provided fields are updated in a single atomic operation. The title field is required and cannot be empty. Optional fields (description, startedAt, dueAt) can be updated or left unchanged.

Every successful edit automatically creates a corresponding entry in the todo's edit history, recording which fields were changed and when. The system verifies that the requesting user owns the todo before processing the update.

Returns the complete updated todo entity with all current field values including timestamps.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Verify the requesting user owns the todo by checking multi_user_todo_member_id matches the authenticated user's ID.

Validate that title is provided and non-empty. Validate optional fields: description (string or null), startedAt (valid date-time or null), dueAt (valid date-time or null).

Update the multi_user_todo_todos record with provided fields. Set updated_at to current timestamp.

Automatically create a new entry in multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories table recording: todo ID, timestamp, and which fields were changed (title, description, started_at, due_at).

Return the complete updated todo entity.

Error cases:
- 404: Todo not found or user doesn't own it
- 400: Validation errors (empty title, invalid date format)
- 403: User not authorized to edit this todo

responseBody.description: The complete updated todo entity with all current field values

requestBody.description: Fields to update: title (required, non-empty), description (optional), startedAt (optional), dueAt (optional)

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before it can be updated - the todoId path parameter references an existing todo entity

operations.description:
Soft delete a todo by moving it to the trash.

This operation marks a todo as deleted by setting its deleted_at timestamp, effectively moving it to the trash. The todo is not permanently removed from the system and retains all its properties including title, description, dates, and completion status. Soft deleted todos no longer appear in the normal todo list but remain accessible through the trash view for potential restoration or permanent deletion.

Only the todo owner can delete their own todos. Attempts to delete todos owned by other users will be rejected. The todo must exist and be in an active (non-deleted) state. Once deleted, the todo can be restored from trash or permanently deleted using trash-specific endpoints.

This operation automatically triggers the creation of an edit history entry recording the deletion event, maintaining an audit trail of all todo modifications.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Soft delete a todo by setting its deleted_at timestamp to the current time.

1. Verify the todo exists and is owned by the current user (match multi_user_todo_member_id to authenticated user's member id)
2. Verify the todo is not already deleted (deleted_at is null)
3. Update the todo's deleted_at field to current timestamp
4. Create an edit history entry in multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories recording the deletion with changed_fields indicating 'deleted_at'
5. Return no response body (204 No Content)

Edge cases:
- Todo not found: Return 404 Not Found
- Todo not owned by user: Return 403 Forbidden
- Todo already deleted: Return 400 Bad Request (todo must be in active state)
- Concurrent modification: Use optimistic locking with updated_at timestamp if needed

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to delete (UUID format, scoped to current user)
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before it can be deleted - the delete operation requires an existing todo resource

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of soft-deleted todos from the user's trash.

This operation provides access to todos that have been deleted by the user but not yet permanently removed. Deleted todos retain all their original attributes including title, description, start date, due date, and completion status. The trash is scoped to the individual user, ensuring privacy isolation - users can only view their own deleted todos.

Supports filtering by completion status and sorting by creation date, start date, or due date. Todos without start or due dates appear at the end when sorting by those fields. Pagination is applied to handle large result sets efficiently.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_todos table with filter deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND multi_user_todo_member_id equals current user's ID.
Apply completion status filter if provided (completed_at IS NULL for incomplete, IS NOT NULL for complete).
Apply sorting based on request parameters: created_at, started_at, or due_at with direction (ASC/DESC).
Handle null started_at and due_at by placing them at the end of sorted results.
Use index on [multi_user_todo_member_id, deleted_at, created_at] for efficient filtering.
Return paginated results with cursor-based or offset-based pagination.
Include total count for pagination metadata.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of deleted todo summaries from the user's trash

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering deleted todos

operations.description:
Restore a deleted todo from the trash back to the active todo list.

This operation allows users to recover their own deleted todos by clearing the soft delete timestamp. The todo returns to its original state with all properties preserved including title, description, dates, and completion status. The original creation date is maintained, and all edit history entries remain accessible.

Only the todo owner can restore their own deleted todos. The operation validates that the todo exists in the user's trash (has a non-null deleted_at timestamp) before allowing restoration. Attempting to restore a todo that is not deleted or does not belong to the user will be rejected.

After successful restoration, the todo reappears in normal todo list queries and can be edited, completed, or deleted again.
operations.name: restore
operations.specification:
Validate that the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated user by checking multi_user_todo_member_id matches the session user.

Verify the todo is in deleted state (deleted_at is not null). Reject if deleted_at is null with 400 Bad Request indicating todo is not in trash.

Clear the deleted_at field by setting it to null to restore the todo to active state.

Preserve all other fields unchanged: title, description, started_at, due_at, completed_at, created_at, updated_at.

Do not create a new edit history entry for the restore operation itself.

Return the full restored todo entity with deleted_at now null.

Handle edge cases: todo not found (404), not owned by user (403), not in trash state (400).

responseBody.description: The restored todo entity with all properties

parameters.description: Todo ID to restore from trash (UUID format)
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before it can be deleted to trash and subsequently restored

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo from the trash, removing it and all associated edit history completely.

This operation permanently removes a todo that is currently in the trash state. Unlike soft deletion which moves todos to trash, this operation completely erases the todo and all its edit history entries from the system. This action cannot be undone.

The todo must be in the deleted state (present in trash) and must be owned by the current user. Attempting to permanently delete a todo that is not in the trash or does not belong to the user will result in an error.

Upon successful deletion, the todo and all related edit history records are cascade deleted from the database.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Permanently delete a todo from trash with cascade deletion of edit history.

1. Verify authentication: Ensure request is from an authenticated member
2. Validate todoId format: Must be a valid UUID
3. Query todo by ID with ownership check: SELECT FROM multi_user_todo_todos WHERE id = {todoId} AND multi_user_todo_member_id = {currentUserId}
4. Verify trash state: Check that deleted_at is NOT NULL (todo must be in trash)
5. If todo not found or not in trash: Return 404 Not Found
6. If todo not owned by user: Return 403 Forbidden
7. Execute cascade delete: DELETE FROM multi_user_todo_todos WHERE id = {todoId}
   - This automatically deletes all related multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories via CASCADE constraint
8. Return 204 No Content on success

Edge cases:
- Todo not in trash (deleted_at is NULL): Reject with 404
- Todo owned by different user: Reject with 403
- Todo already permanently deleted: Return 404
- Invalid UUID format: Return 400 Bad Request

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to permanently delete (scoped to current user's trash)
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before it can be permanently deleted from trash

operations.description:
Retrieve the edit history of a specific todo with pagination and sorting capabilities.

This operation returns a chronological list of all edit history entries for the specified todo, showing what fields were changed and when. Each history entry captures the new values of modified fields (title, description, started_at, due_at) along with the timestamp of when the edit was made.

History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest by default. Supports pagination for todos with extensive edit history. Users can only access the edit history of their own todos - attempting to access another user's todo history will be rejected.

Edit history is automatically created whenever a todo is successfully edited. Failed edit operations do not create history entries. When a todo is permanently deleted from trash, its entire edit history is also permanently deleted.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories table filtered by multi_user_todo_todo_id parameter.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated user (check multi_user_todo_member_id matches current user)
2. Query edit histories where multi_user_todo_todo_id equals the path parameter
3. Apply sorting by created_at DESC (most recent first) by default
4. Support pagination with page and take parameters
5. Support optional filtering by date range (created_at from/to)
6. Return summary fields: id, created_at, title, description, started_at, due_at
7. Include pagination metadata in response

Authorization: Member actor only. Reject if todo does not belong to authenticated user.
Error handling: Return 404 if todo not found or does not belong to user. Return 403 if user lacks permission.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo edit history entries in summary format

parameters.description: Todo identifier (UUID format, scoped to current user's todos)
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Pagination and filtering parameters for edit history search

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before its edit history can be retrieved, as edit history entries are child resources that reference the parent todo via foreign key

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific edit history entry from the multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories table.

This operation returns detailed information about a single edit made to a todo, including the timestamp of when the edit was made and the new values of any fields that were changed. Only fields that were actually modified during the edit will have values; unchanged fields will be null.

Users can only access edit history entries for todos they own through the multi_user_todo_todos relationship. The history entry includes the edit timestamp and any changed field values (title, description, started_at, due_at). Edit histories are cascade deleted when the parent todo is permanently removed.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories table by history ID.

First verify the todo exists and belongs to the current user by checking multi_user_todo_todo_id matches a todo owned by the authenticated member. This prevents unauthorized access to another user's todo history.

Return the full history entry with all fields: id, created_at timestamp, and the optional changed field values (title, description, started_at, due_at). Only fields that were actually modified during the edit will contain values; others will be null.

Return 404 if the history entry does not exist or if the todo does not belong to the current user.

responseBody.description: The requested edit history entry with timestamp and changed field values

parameters.description: Todo ID (UUID format, identifies the parent todo)
parameters.name: todoId

parameters.description: History entry ID (UUID format, identifies the specific edit)
parameters.name: historyId

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before edit history entries can exist, as history entries reference todos via foreign key multi_user_todo_todo_id

Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When

Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

Title is required when provided (minLength: 1). Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are auto-managed. Owner FK (multi_user_todo_member_id) resolved from JWT. Completion status (completed_at) and soft-delete (deleted_at) handled by separate endpoints. Edit history auto-generated on successful update.

displayName.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from multi_user_todo_user_profiles.display_name. User's public display name shown throughout the application.

createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from multi_user_todo_user_profiles.created_at. Set automatically when profile is created.

updatedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from multi_user_todo_user_profiles.updated_at. Updated automatically on each profile modification.

deletedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from multi_user_todo_user_profiles.deleted_at. Nullable - null when profile is active, contains timestamp when soft deleted.

IMultiUserTodoUserProfile.description: User profile entity containing the user's public display name shown in the application interface and metadata timestamps for creation, update, and soft deletion. Returned when retrieving or updating the current authenticated member's profile.
IMultiUserTodoUserProfile.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from multi_user_todo_user_profiles table. Properties id, displayName, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt map directly to DB columns. The multi_user_todo_member_id FK is resolved from JWT session context and not exposed in the response. Profile is accessed via authenticated member session - the member relation is not included as this DTO represents the profile entity itself.

IMultiUserTodoGuest.ISummary.description: Summary view of a guest account with essential identification and timestamp information. Used in session listings to show associated guest details.
IMultiUserTodoGuest.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from multi_user_todo_guests table. All scalar columns included: id (UUID), device_fingerprint (string), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at (nullable). Excluded: sessions HAS-MANY relation (composition, separate endpoint). All timestamps in ISO 8601 date-time format.

IMultiUserTodoMember.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary view of a member account. Contains the member's unique identifier and public display name for ownership attribution in todo and session responses.
IMultiUserTodoMember.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Summary DTO for member ownership references. Direct mapping: id from multi_user_todo_members.id. Computed via JOIN: displayName from multi_user_todo_user_profiles.display_name (separate table, JOIN on member id). Excluded: email (privacy), password_hash (security), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (internal metadata), sessions/passwordResets/emailVerifications/profile/todos (aggregation relations not included in summary).
